hypothesis: A direct CP-SAT model with integer marks and all 105 difference variables constrained by a global AllDifferent constraint can find a scope-111 DTS even though the tested heuristic families do not.
rationale: The true DTS condition is a finite integer constraint system; a solver formulation removes heuristic basin and irreversible-choice effects while preserving the exact target.
expected_information_gain: Returns either an independently validated scope-111 witness or a time-bounded solver status/bound that characterizes whether this compact formulation is computationally viable.
method: Build 42 integer mark variables with normalized strict row order and scope <=111, 105 exact difference variables in [1,111], global AllDifferent, and safe first-mark row symmetry. Solve with OR-Tools CP-SAT 9.15.6755 using 8 workers and a fixed seed.
metric: CP-SAT feasibility status and independently verified DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A FEASIBLE solution accepted by the independent integer validator is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness; UNKNOWN/timeout is solver evidence only and not a mathematical infeasibility result.
kill_condition: Stop after 120 seconds or immediately on a complete solution that passes the independent validator; do not interpret UNKNOWN as infeasibility.

raw_result.error: Windows fatal exception: access violation in ortools.sat.python.cp_model.CpSolver.solve
raw_result.control_sanity: same crash on three-variable AllDifferent with one worker and one second

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if FEASIBLE and validator-valid

interpretation: The exact constraint model could not obtain a solver status because the installed OR-Tools native runtime crashes on solve even for a three-variable control model. This is a runtime blocker, not evidence of DTS infeasibility.
what_was_learned: CP-SAT cannot be used in the current native Windows environment without changing runtime/dependency conditions; no DTS metric movement was measured.
recommended_next_action: Do not retest CP-SAT in this runtime. Use an upstream-inspired block-deletion bitmask search that remains executable in pure Python, or resume CP-SAT only in Linux.
